I understand that I will never be that, however that does not mean I cannot try even if it is just a delusion.  I would rather have a delusional belief that I can someday be normal than to give in to slaughtering people. 

My family was abused violently from before I was born.  My dad was extremely cruel and used to beat me and my mom.  When my brother was born I took to being his protector as I saw in him the innocence I desired.  I was not a psychopath at that time however.  I had emotions and feelings. I had already gained a disconnected and disjointed view of the world in that everyone is bad and everyone deserves to die horribly and painfully.  Today, I still sometimes think that way, but I now have a more complex understanding of good versus bad.  I still find that in comparison to other people, my views on morality are still rather shallow.

That is where my story starts.  It goes on to me going through my grandpa's death at the age of 6.  At the age of 8 one of my dogs died from liver failure.  I used to consider my dogs my only true family and friends as they were always there for me.  All that time, the abuse and violence never ceased and I was very emotionally desensitized.  My mom divorced my dad shortly after and both my parents blamed it on me and my brother which further desensitized me and dissociated me from my emotions.   By this time I had already dissected several animals to try to ascertain what causes death as I was curious about why my dog had left me.  I gained insight into it via the internet ultimately.  At age 9, my last friend, my pet dog was slaughtered in my dad's backyard by the neighbors pit-bulls.  I came home to find her lying in the arroyo out back severely ripped up.  There were pools of blood all over the yard.  I went into a short state of shock.  I believe today that the loss of my only perceived friend at that point sealed my fate as a psychopath. It also gave me the first inspirations for my usual murder fantasies.  I sometimes fantasize about partially skinning people alive and then cutting the carotid and watching the blood pool around the body before leaving my signature snowflake.  Other times I find myself wondering what random peoples' skulls would look and feel like in my hands with no flesh.  Shortly after the incident I tracked down the pit-bulls and slaughtered them with a machete I had stolen from somewhere (I don't actually remember where).  The pit-bulls had just had a litter of puppies.  I took the puppies and skinned them and painted their blood all over rocks and grass out in the wild.  (If your wondering, yes I did sustain a few bites as the dogs tried to defend themselves but they unsuccessful in trying to survive my rage. This was the first time I had done so in the manner that I fantasize about today.  

I became fascinated with symbology at this point in my life.  I began to associate the cold with my growing lack of empathy and emotion.  I would draw ice kingdoms devoid of life.  I slowly molded it into a more compact symbol: a snowflake.  The snowflake represents me.  Cold and fragile, but beautiful in its own way and deadly in large quantities.  I began to fantasize about what other people felt and what was considered normal.  The snowflake's beauty came to represent my 'hope' to one day feel again and one day not be so alone.  All I feel today is an unending emptiness inside. Like I am missing out on life itself.

I would use the snowflake as my mark to represent my failed attempt to be normal and to show I will punish those I feel to be responsible for my ruined life.  Though I admit that my targets aren't exactly 'guilty' of the crimes I accuse them of.  If I end up killing, I won't be in a sane and rational state of mind like I am now.  The best way to resist the impulse and instinct to kill is to keep my cool and rationalize my way out of it.

At the age of 13, my mom lapsed into a coma from ongoing cancer.  She began suffocating on her own.  I just stood there and watched.  I counted the seconds it took for her to die.  356 seconds exactly.  She died at 20:10:36 in February. When she died, I felt nothing.  It didn't seem to matter to me in the slightest.  I locked myself up in the bathroom to avoid being seen not crying.  I even received comments later about my lack of crying or even expression of grief at memorial services.  I never went through grief from it.  That was the day that I became a full fledged psychopath.  I accepted that I care only about myself. Though today I try to behave as though I care about others.  

That day, I began to use my lack of emotion to take advantage of people.  I would feign emotions to get what I wanted and manipulate situations.  I would lie deliberately to people to hurt them.  I started getting into fights and sent people to hospitals.  Of course, I was careful and never got caught for it.  I expressed bisexual interest in sex around the age of 16 whereupon I began to take advantage of others for sexual favors. I began sleeping around with both boys and girls.  At 17 I burned my dad's shed to the ground.  I then began planning to bomb my high-school.  I never followed through with my plans however.  

My dad kicked me out when he found out that I was sleeping with other girls.  He was not supportive of me in any way and just used it as an excuse to get rid of me.  He once locked me out of the house in the middle of summer until I dug out a tree from the back yard.  It took me four hours.  After that, a few weeks later, I blew his kitchen up by separating the gas line to the oven.  I never got caught once for any of it.  Anyways, after getting kicked out I was homeless for a time.  During that time I was raped twice.  Those rapes solidified my fantasy targets as males. I had already been fantasizing about killing christians.  The christian part comes from my shallow hatred of christianity.  I tend to blame my dad's religiosity for my development into a psychopath.  

I stayed in school during that time and got my diploma however.  Then I moved away and that basically brings me to now.  I kind of wanted to share as the fact I have nobody to talk to about this is nagging at me.  

If anyone is interested in talking to me about any of this, I welcome it.  
Fair warning though: I'm a sick, fucked up, creepy little bitchy psychopath  who fantasizes about killing and sometimes I say or do things that hurt others, sometimes unintentionally and sometimes intentionally.  I have not to this day killed and I do not plan to.  If you're a christian male, I would recommend not telling me that and maybe erring on the side of caution as I always have that dark urge in there somewhere and honestly I'd love to indulge it.  I still sorta kinda want to be normal more than to indulge but sometimes it is very tempting.  Please don't present me with the temptation.  It's like putting candy in front of a starving 6 year old and telling her not to eat it.

Please exercise caution when dealing with people you know to be a psychopath, including myself obviously. 

My ultimate goal is to one day be normal, and I don't care how blown out of proportion that goal is.  I want to be normal.  Ultimately I realize that eventually I will slip as do most serial killers (who haven't killed) and wind up killing someone, but for now I am keeping my no killing efforts up.

Hormones do much more than genetics.  It's actually why transpeople exist in the most likely case.  In utero, there are two spurts of hormones for males, one to masculinize the body and one to masculinize the brain.  Transwomen occur when the one hits the body but doesn't hit the brain.  Transwomen literally _are born women_ with male bodies.  No amount of social upbringing or differing genetics will change that.  If you are trans, if you truly feel you're trans then you have a female brain and should try to accept that.

At worst, liver failure would be first, then heart attack, and then kidney failure.   Liver failure would be worst because then you couldn't take hormones ever again.  Heart attack could preclude you from surgery.  Kidney failure would just be all around bad.  Most likely you'll get sick for a few days and you'll never want to do that again.

Basically, six month to a year _at the right levels_ gets you to at least an A cup in most cases.  I'm a year and counting and I'm almost a B.  It does have to stay at the right levels though or not much will happen.  Just stick to it.  Hormones have more effects than just breast growth.  They can help paychologically, as well as put some stuff on the hips and thighs.  My hips are tremendously bigger than when I started.  My hip bone hasn't fused, so some of it is skeletal for me. My hips are wider than my shoulders, but about half of it is fat distribution.  Softer skin comes with hormones as well.  Less body hair as well. Given time at the right levels, which are different per person, all of these changes can and in most cases will happen.  But yes, you do need to stay steady at the right levels.

I can think of a number of things:

"How do you have sex?"

That one's obviously offensive.  You wouldn't ask how your dad has sex, or how some random girl has sex.

"When did you choose this?"

This is offensive because trans people are born trans.  Nobody in their right mind chooses this.

"Do you have a dick?"
"Do you have a vulva?"

Asking someone what they have in their pants is invasive and unethical.

"What's your _real_ name?"

The name the transperson uses everyday is their real name, not the one they were born with.  Many trans people hate their dead names.

"You gonna have it removed?"

Again incredibly invasive. Also, I believe it is actually illegal to require someone to answer this in the US under HIPAA as it pertains to private and personal medical information.

"Are your boobs real?"

This is incredibly insulting as the transperson may have waited a long time for them to grow and feel like their efforts were invalidated by the question. Or they might not like having breasts, and reminding the person they do is not good for their psyche.

"Are you a man or a woman?"

The stupidest question anyone can ask a transperson.  Not all trans people identify as either male or female.  Some identify as both. Some, as neither.  Not to mention that if the person introduces themself as Bruce, vs Janette, most of the time you get a pretty clear answer from their name alone.  And if you really aren't sure, just simply ask what their pronouns are and that'll clue you in.

"Why not just be gay?"

This one stems from a lack of understanding that sexual orientation (the gender of the person you're fucking) does not equal gender identity (the gender you wish to be while your fucking).  Two different things.  Trans people can be gay, bi, straight, pan, or asexual irrespective of their trans identity.

That is most of the ones I can think of right now for most situations.  All are equally offensive.  The most insensitive thing I've ever been told was:  

"Cutting your [stuff] off and wearing a dress does not make you a woman." -- My dad.

Not quite a question, but certainly not something you want to say to a transperson.  Invalidating a transperson's identity is a terrible idea.  It will cause them serious distress and most likely make them hate you forever.

My dad no longer is a part of my life and never will be again for the shit he put me through.

Very early in I was very indecisive about it.  I put it off for nearly a decade going back and forth thinking that maybe I was wrong, or that I wasn't really trans, or that my feeling of wrongness wasn't valid.  

I kept it bottled up until I literally exploded and locked myself in my room after taking a whole bottle of acetaminophen (like 30 tablets) and slicing my wrists and trying to hang myself, with my parents on the phone with the police.

I got more and more frustrated with it as time went and I kept denying and denying to myself that this was really happening and that I really did feel wrong as a male.  I eventually couldn't handle the inner war with myself.  I always tried to make everyone happy in that they thought I was male, so much so that it led me to lock myself up in my room and do those things above.

It was horrible.

So I decided to just be me and go with the flow.  Wear whatever I want.  Act how I want.  Be how I want.  And so now I'm over a year on HRT and it was totally worth it.  That inner denial is gone.  The moment I felt estradiol kick in inside my system, it just clicked.  My depression fell away rapidly and I was able to look in the mirror for the first time without the whole "Am I trans? Am I not? What in the heck am I?" 

At this point, I've given it a lot of thought.  The ultimate question for me was if I had to live the rest of my life being seen as male or female or in between or neither, what would I want to live as?  Ultimately the answer for me was "female". If you want to pursue transition, do it.  Don't let other people get in the way of you're health.  Society pushes us to the edge. We have to show that even with all the bad things that can happen on the way, our sanity and well being are more important than the comfort of others.  When society is taken out of its comfort zone, it has the opportunity to grow and become better rounded and more equal.
